items.title: Environmental Emergencies: Heat, Part 2
items.summary: The second half of the Sydney HEMS heat package, landing the week before the Australian summer it is written for.

_homepage.note: Part 1 went up four days ago; this instalment carries three recorded talks, including A/Prof Lai Heng Fong on heat exposure and heat illness in both patients and staff, and former ACEM President Simon Judkins on climate as a health emergency. It is tagged to the PHRM curriculum point 1.2.17, so it doubles as exam-shaped material. Heat presentations are a Victorian summer problem that arrives in the ED in clusters rather than singly, which is exactly what the staff-exposure half of this is about.

items.title: David Axelrod :: S/T
items.summary: A long look at the Axelrod self-titled, which is the hinge between the 60s soul-jazz production world and everything that sampled it.

_homepage.note: Axelrod sits directly behind a good part of the shelf — his arranging and production work is the connective tissue between the Capitol soul-jazz era and the Curtis Mayfield and Parliament end of the collection, and the drum sound here is the one that Menahan Street Band and the whole Daptone orbit spent the 2000s rebuilding. Aquarium Drunkard is good on this kind of record precisely because it treats the production as the subject rather than trivia. If the Mel Brown and Milt Jackson records get played, this is upstream of both.

items.title: Intermittent or Continuous RRT in Acute Kidney Injury
items.summary: A non-inferiority trial that failed to show intermittent haemodialysis is as good as CRRT, which is the opposite of the pragmatic answer most units want.

_homepage.note: The primary outcome was MAKE90 at 78.1% with intermittent haemodialysis against 71.6% with CRRT, and the authors could not declare non-inferiority. That matters at registrar level because the intermittent option is the one that gets reached for when CRRT capacity or nursing ratios are the constraint, and this is the appraisal that tells you what you are trading away. The Bottom Line's structured format gets you to the internal-validity problems faster than the paper does.

items.title: Miles Davis: Copenhagen Live 1969
items.summary: A new 2LP of the lost-quintet year, caught working out Bitches Brew material live before the studio version existed.

_homepage.note: 1969 is the gap in most Miles collections: after the second quintet, before the studio electric records, documented almost entirely by live tapes. This set is the band taking the Bitches Brew book apart in front of an audience, which is a different and rougher thing than the record. Against the straight-ahead end of the shelf — Night Train, Stan Getz, the Milt Jackson and Ray Charles meeting — it is the obvious next step rather than a sideways one.

items.title: RRL — History, Philosophy, and Iconic Products
items.summary: The long version of where RRL came from and why its garments are built the way they are, rather than a product round-up.

_homepage.note: RRL is one of the reference points the whole vintage-and-rustic side of the wardrobe is measured against, and this is the piece that explains the line as a deliberate archive project — the Double RL ranch, the vintage sourcing, the decision to reproduce construction rather than cite it. Useful when you are looking at a secondhand piece and trying to work out which era of the line it belongs to. Heddels is reliably better on provenance than on new-season copy.

items.title: Atelectasis — Internet Book of Critical Care
items.summary: Farkas on the diagnosis everyone writes on the chart and almost nobody works up properly.

_homepage.note: A new IBCC chapter on the thing that explains a third of the hypoxia in a ventilated patient and gets blamed for the other two thirds. Worth reading against the CCPU lung material specifically: atelectasis versus consolidation versus effusion is the discrimination the probe is actually being asked to make, and the chapter is explicit about what recruitment does and does not fix. IBCC entries on PE, VBG and the CBC have already earned their place here.

items.title: Casual Craft: How a Real McCoy's Leather Jacket Is Made
items.summary: Construction walk-through of the most obsessive reproduction house in menswear, step by step rather than brand story.

_homepage.note: Real McCoy's reproduce mid-century American outerwear down to the hide selection and the thread, and Crompton's Casual Craft series is the one corner of Permanent Style that leaves tailoring alone and looks at how a jacket is actually put together. This is the vocabulary that makes a vintage Woolrich or a Pendleton legible — what a sewn-through seam costs, why horsehide behaves differently from steerhide. Pairs with the RRL piece as the two halves of the same question.

items.title: Dragonwilds 1.0.2.2 Live on November 18
items.summary: The hotfix that follows the Luminance-adjacent 1.0.2 drop, aimed at the audio failures and the doors.

_homepage.note: This is the patch after the big one: Armour of the Earth fixes, the audio dropouts, and the door and window interaction bugs that 1.0.2 introduced alongside Earth Magic. Jagex has since said 2027 will be weighted toward stability over new content, which makes this the shape of things for a while. MP1st lists the actual changes rather than summarising the announcement, which is what you want before loading a save.

items.title: PPP Cameras' Pierro Pozella ceases camera repairs
items.summary: One of the few repairers taking in ordinary film cameras is closing that side of the business, which narrows the options for anyone shooting old gear.

_homepage.note: Pozella became the public face of film camera repair through The Repair Shop, and the practical consequence of this is that the queue for competent mechanical servicing gets longer again. He is keeping the refurbished-camera sales and PPP Film Lab going, so the news is narrower than it first reads. Still the sort of thing worth knowing before a shutter starts dragging and the plan was to send it somewhere.

items.title: 5 Frames with Kodak Vision 3 AHU 320D
items.summary: A cine stock shot as a still film, with the remjet question answered rather than hand-waved.

_homepage.note: AHU 320D is the anti-halation-undercoat version of Kodak's tungsten-era cine stock, which is the whole point: no remjet to strip, so an ordinary C-41 lab will take it without ruining the run. 35mmc's 5 Frames format is short enough to be useful — you see what the stock does with daylight and with mixed light, not a datasheet. Worth knowing about while colour negative prices keep climbing.

items.title: Is Victoria's election tackling the big issues?
items.summary: Victorians vote tomorrow, and this is the piece that asks whether the campaign engaged with health at all or just priced it.

_homepage.note: Both majors have put money on the table — Labor's $1.5 billion over four years to expand twelve emergency departments including the Alfred and the Austin, the Coalition's $99 million patient transit lounge fund aimed squarely at ramping. This weighs that against the mental health system and the royal commission's unfinished recommendations, which is where the argument actually is. One in three Victorian ED patients is not being treated within the recommended time, so whichever way Saturday goes, the department he works in is the thing being voted on.

items.title: First Look: Lucky Coq Reopens as Lucky's
items.summary: A Chapel Street fixture reopens tonight after a serious renovation and a name change.

_homepage.note: Lucky Coq ran for two decades as the cheap-pizza-and-long-afternoon option on Chapel Street; this is the first look at what the renovation did to it and whether the $4 pizza logic survived. Opens Friday 27 November, so it is a this-weekend decision rather than a note for later. Southside rather than the usual Brunswick-to-Thornbury run, which makes it worth the trip or worth skipping on the strength of the pictures.
